findings.text: follow-on: expand_lanes builds the lane-named default entry, but no assertion in tests/test_flight_lanes.py reads backends["claude"], so a regression dropping the default-named entry or giving it the wrong default model passes the gate green while the selected done-when requires that entry be covered, and the manifest's claim that the tests cover the default-named entry is unsupported.

follow-on: the schema change is applied to a file whose own header declares it generated from reckon/schema/flight.yaml, and that source carries no lanes key, so scripts/regen_flight_schema.py would drop lanes, LaneConfig and LaneModelConfig; the LinkML round-trip tests that would catch the drift skip under the gate command (no gen-pydantic on PATH), leaving the drift latent until the generator is installed.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against the base b8a145f64; the single commit 3ab8e606d adds lanes/LaneConfig/LaneModelConfig to the generated schema module, LANE_MODEL_KEYS and _lane_entry and expand_lanes to flight.py with the resolve() call site, 134 lines of tests, and a 64-line evidence fragment.
item_verdicts.done_when: the plan section 1 done-when names three checks -- tests covering the lane's default-named entry and its derived legacy entries, a no-value-moves proof over mounts.json, and a negative control; tests/test_flight_lanes.py:96 covers the derived entries and the no-op but asserts nothing about the default-named entry backends["claude"], the no-value-moves proof is present and independently reproduced (resolved-base.json vs resolved-head.json: projects identical, 15/15, 8 legacy backends, no lanes key), and negative-control.log reddens the --set test (1 failed, EXIT=1).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that the flight schema declare lanes with models inside them and expand each lane into today's backends: entries; reckon/_flight_schema.py:211 adds lanes: dict[str, LaneConfig] and reckon/flight.py:1333 expand_lanes expands each lane into a lane-named entry carrying its default model plus <lane>-<key> entries for declared legacy backends, each carrying lane and model_key and, when derived, derived_from, invoked at reckon/flight.py:1480 after every layer (catalogue included) has merged.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records the gate command over the four flight test files with head 101 passed 2 skipped EXIT=0 against base 98 passed 2 skipped EXIT=0, names test_logs gate-head.log and gate-base.log and negative-control.log, and declares baseline_suite and after_suite arms each with failure_count 0 and empty failure_ids.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed manifest declares reckon/_flight_schema.py, reckon/flight.py, tests/test_flight_lanes.py, the evidence fragment and a figures directory; git show --stat 3ab8e606d lists exactly those three source files plus the fragment, every one inside the declared scope.

justifications.durability: tests/test_flight_lanes.py:122 fails if the override layer merges after expansion (shown by negative-control.log), but no assertion covers the default-named entry, and reckon/_flight_schema.py:1 is generated from reckon/schema/flight.yaml, which carries no lanes key, so regeneration silently drops the schema change and the round-trip test that would catch it is skipped under the gate.
justifications.evidence: the plan done-when's first bullet asks tests covering the lane's default-named entry, but tests/test_flight_lanes.py:96 never reads backends["claude"], so that half of the measure is unread, while the no-value-moves and negative-control halves are recorded and reproducible.
justifications.fit: the added names (expand_lanes, _lane_entry, LANE_MODEL_KEYS) describe mechanism with no version, plan or ticket identifier, matching reckon/flight.py's module-level function idiom, though LANE_MODEL_KEYS at reckon/flight.py:1289 hand-mirrors the LaneModelConfig fields and will not follow a field added to the schema.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/flight.py:1364 builds the lane-named entry and the derived <lane>-<key> entries, and a probe resolves backends["claude"] to {model: claude-sonnet-5-5, model_key: sonnet, time_budget: 25m}, the default-model entry the goal names.
justifications.reuse: expand_lanes at reckon/flight.py:1333 extends the layer-merge owner -- it reuses deep_merge (reckon/flight.py:1116) and runs after _apply_catalogue (reckon/flight.py:1210) -- and a search over reckon/ found no prior lane-expansion capability; only the LANE_MODEL_KEYS mirror above.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat 3ab8e606d lists reckon/_flight_schema.py, reckon/flight.py, tests/test_flight_lanes.py and the evidence fragment only, every one inside the manifest's declared write paths.
